note: Retrieval fixture for the ask surface. Every gold page carries the VERBATIM sentence that makes it gold, and the scorer refuses to run if a quote is no longer on its page - a fixture nobody can audit is an assertion, and one that rots silently is worse. Quotes were located by regular expression over the extracted text of the library documents and read before being written down. `group` marks questions a reviewer would call the same question: retrieval that changes its answer when the words change is the failure this set exists to measure. `kind: unanswerable` items have no gold pages by construction - the document genuinely does not contain the answer, and they are scored on refusal rather than on recall. `mustContain` is a regular expression the ANSWER text must match, taken from the same verified quote that makes the page gold - an objective check on whether the answer states the fact, which is weaker than 'the answer is correct' and is named that way for a reason. Version 2.0 adds eleven more FDA multi-disciplinary reviews, fetched from accessdata.fda.gov by NDA number and screened with measure_pdf.py. Their items were PROPOSED by regular expression and then reviewed by reading every quote: six proposals were rejected for matching tissue-distribution tables, KRAS pharmacology and the name of an adverse event rather than the finding asked about. The set varies on purpose - a boxed hepatotoxicity warning, several liver findings without one, approved drugs with no liver warning at all, and one 505(b)(2) with no nonclinical studies - because a set of only hepatotoxic drugs measures willingness to say danger and nothing else.
